page: Microsoft Azure D32d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced compute, memory, and direct-attached storage requirements. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, this instance allocates 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU features 35 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware support for instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The system provides 128 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of the DDv4 series.

A key differentiator of the D32d_v4 instance is its integrated local storage, supplying 1,288 GB of direct-attached solid-state drive capacity. This storage delivers high-speed temporary volume space suitable for low-latency scratch disks, paging, and ephemeral database caches without relying solely on network-attached block devices. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units, relying entirely on the central processing units for compute execution.

Benchmark assessments show the instance performing consistently within the median 50 percent across most CPU and system workloads. It recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,781.0 alongside a single-core score of 1,275.0, reflecting steady middle-tier compute output. Memory throughput tests demonstrated large-block read rates of 105.49 GB/sec and write rates of 46.46 GB/sec. Application testing indicated steady transactional performance, highlighted by 26.79 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.26 GB/sec throughput in static web serving. A single-threaded gzip compression result of 23.49 GB/sec fell into the lower quartile, and large 70B LLM prompt processing registered a low 4.65 tokens per second.

By delivering a solid 4 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside an expansive 1,288 GB local SSD, the D32d_v4 offers strong resource density without requiring excessive storage add-on allocations. It serves well for enterprise relational databases, distributed microservices, static web infrastructure, intermediate ETL pipelines, and Redis in-memory caching tiers requiring local persistent swap space.
description: Microsoft Azure D32d_v4 is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 32 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM, backed by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor with AVX-512 extensions. Maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration is complemented by 1,288 GB of local SSD storage for low-latency ephemeral data operations. Benchmark evaluations place the server within the mid-range across core compute, system memory bandwidth, and caching operations, achieving 26.79 million Redis SET operations per second and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 10,781. While single-threaded compression and massive large-language model processing highlight compute boundaries, the bundled high-capacity local disk and symmetrical hardware balance make it an efficient host for enterprise relational databases, Redis caching layers, web application tiers, and multi-threaded enterprise workloads.
